evidence: Version 2 resolves the 'Glacier Meltwater Basin' concept more cleanly: the matte ice sheet reads as a continuous平面 sweeping to a low, calm horizon with a believable turquoise meltwater caustic band drifting at the horizon line, matching the declared palette (#e6eeef ice, #37b0c4 caustics, #12333c type). The bottle sits left of centre with a soft contact shadow absorbed at its foot, so physical contact is convincing under the diffuse high-key polar light; the saturated ocean-blue glass still reads backlit against the frozen white matte. The right-hand column is coherent and hierarchical: DAVIDOFF at column head, 'Cool / Water' across two tall lines, EAU DE TOILETTE and the short glacier rule closing the column, with wide horizontal clearance from the cap zone. Version 1 by contrast uses busy diagonal marbled streaks that cut across the bottle's base and behind the type column, weakening ground contact, horizon calm and column clearance; its ice texture reads as decorative veining rather than meltwater caustics. Neither version shows studio equipment or floating-packshot defects, and product fidelity (silhouette, opaque cap, white print) is intact in both, so the calmer, better-grounded set wins.
remaining_problems: Title sets in a regular-weight sans rather than a truly condensed Arial Narrow cut; the 'two tall condensed lines' read wider than the brief's column spec.
Turquoise caustic ripples concentrate in a horizon band and do not visibly drift across the foreground ice or the pale mist sky above, partially under-delivering the declared light movement.
Contact shadow at the bottle foot is very faint; grounding is plausible but could absorb slightly more to anchor the packshot on the matte ice.
The glacier rule and EAU DE TOILETTE line sit close to the caustic band, slightly muddying the column's closing whitespace against the horizon.
